archetype: BG -1/-1 counter aristocrats. deck-audit takes the frame's `combo` archetype and applies its overrides (tutors 4-8, protection 4-6); the deck meets both, at 8 tutors and 5 protection. But the measured behaviour is a converter engine, not a combo deck: 25 creatures, modal mana value 2, a 67.2% commander-plus-payoff assembly, and a headline kill that assembles 16.3% of the time. The frame's own line — 'a genuine but narrow combo ceiling sits above a grindy median' — is what the numbers show.
verdict: This deck starts better than almost anything in the fleet: 36 land copies, zero unconditional taplands, 15 colour sources above Karsten's worst-colour target, a 90.2% turn-3 land drop and a commander on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs. Its payoff class (6), converter class (4) and tutor class (8) are all deep, and it out-draws a table. What binds is the one class no axis measures: a repeatable, non-combat -1/-1 counter SOURCE. Four of the six cards in the payoff component — Hapatra herself, Nest of Scarabs, Flourishing Defenses and Obelisk Spider — do nothing at all until a -1/-1 counter is placed; only the three death-drains run off a plain sacrifice. After stack 001 the deck holds exactly one free repeatable source — Yawgmoth, Thran Physician — while the audit's two flagged single points of failure are one card each at 7.1% of an opening seven. Second, and compounding it: the engine is entirely creature-activated-ability based and the deck answers exactly one permanent class.

components.reading: Six deep, 36.4% of an opening seven, and assembled with the commander 67.2% of the time at mean turn 3.623. The abundant half.
The drain converters, four deep, 51.9% assembled. Blood Artist drains one player per death; the other three hit each opponent.
Five free sacrifice outlets, 31.2% of an opening seven. Not thin — but stack 001 refuted the Mikaeus pairing for all five of them, so this component's declared job no longer exists.
Eight tutors, 45.6% of an opening seven, 78% drawn. This is the deck's substitute for redundancy in the classes that have none.
One card. 7.1% of an opening seven, 16.3% assembled beside the commander. The deck's headline two-card kill, and deck-audit's closer search found no pool card that joins it by role or by combo line.
One card, at six mana, assembled 9.5% of the time. The audit surfaces 8 combo lines that would join it (of 75 candidates), every one of them unverified.

UNDECLARED — goldfish_targets.json names no counter-source component, so nothing measures the class every payoff depends on. Yawgmoth is the deck's only free repeatable non-combat source (stack 001's outlet census, checker-verified); Devoted Druid sources only onto itself and needs Mikaeus to survive doing it.

single_points_of_failure.component: ignition — a repeatable, non-combat -1/-1 counter source
single_points_of_failure.why: Four of the six payoff-component cards trigger only on counter placement — Nest of Scarabs ('Whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature, create that many 1/1 black Insect creature tokens'), Flourishing Defenses ('Whenever a -1/-1 counter is put on a creature'), Obelisk Spider, and Hapatra's own token half. They cannot start themselves. The other three, Blood Artist / Zulaport Cutthroat / Bastion of Remembrance, drain on any death and do run off a plain sacrifice outlet — so it is the body-generating half of the deck, and its whole -1/-1 identity, that is gated here. The deck's other placements are one-shots (Fume Spitter, Grim Affliction, Black Sun's Zenith), combat-gated (Hapatra's own first ability, Obelisk Spider, Necroskitter's wither), or metered (Serrated Arrows, three uses; Contagion Clasp, {4} a proliferate). That leaves Yawgmoth, which stack 001 also showed needs a second body every activation. The audit has no axis for this class, so the deck's 16 numbers cannot see the thing that binds it.

cut_candidates.why: It is the only card in the deck that kills creatures without placing a counter. 'All creatures get -X/-X until end of turn' triggers none of the six payoffs, makes no Snakes, no Insects and no Elf Warriors, leaves nothing for Crumbling Ashes or Necroskitter, and eats your own fodder — 3.162 bodies on board by turn 6. Black Sun's Zenith sits beside it doing the same job and paying you for it.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: The deck loses its cheapest sweeper and its only answer to a resolved fatty at three mana. Toxic Deluge is three mana for any X because X is paid in life; Black Sun's Zenith needs X+2 mana for the same X, which at turn 5's mean 5.497 available mana is X=3. That is a real efficiency loss and it is the strongest argument against this cut. Sweepers drops 2 to 1, still inside the cited 1-3 band, and against an indestructible board you now have nothing.

open_questions.question: Does the Blowfly family loop? Blowfly Infestation paired with Hapatra, with Nest of Scarabs, and with Flourishing Defenses are three of the nineteen claimed two-card infinites, and the pairing with Hapatra is the deck's declared headline kill that goldfish measures at 16.3%. No stack artifact touches any of them. A scenario must settle whether the loop is optional enough to avoid a draw, whether it needs a seed counter and a spare body, and what happens when no legal target remains.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the single thinnest declared component in the deck and its status is unknown. A pilot is currently being asked to mulligan toward a line nobody has adjudicated.

open_questions.question: Does Mikaeus, the Unhallowed switch the token loops OFF? His anthem makes non-Human tokens — Snakes, Insects, Elf Warriors — 2/2, so a single -1/-1 counter no longer takes them to 0 toughness. If that holds, the deck's two flagship engines are mutually exclusive on the battlefield.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether Mikaeus is a combo piece or an anti-synergy, and therefore whether a six-mana single point of failure belongs in a deck whose modal mana value is 2. Stack 001 step 15 already showed his anthem changes exactly this arithmetic for Walking Ballista.

open_questions.question: Does the Ivy Lane family work? Scurry Oak + Ivy Lane Denizen is bracket_report's highest-bracket line, and six further entries pair Ivy Lane with a sacrifice outlet that makes no green creature enter. Verify the Scurry Oak pairing; audit the other six.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Seven of the eleven unadjudicated lines sit here, and the Scurry Oak cut proposed above should not be applied until this returns.

open_questions.question: Does Yawgmoth + Hapatra loop without Mikaeus, and what bounds it? Sacrifice a Snake, place the counter on a creature that survives it, Hapatra mints a replacement Snake — net body count flat, one card drawn and one life paid per activation.
open_questions.why_it_matters: On the evidence this is the line the deck actually wins with most often, it needs neither of the six-mana pieces, and it has never been resolved. Stack 001 verified Yawgmoth's mechanics only inside the Mikaeus line.

open_questions.question: Should goldfish_targets.json declare a counter-SOURCE component, and should the 'Mikaeus + a free sacrifice outlet' target be retired? All five outlets in that target's any_of group — Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Blasting Station — are on stack 001's refuted list, so the simulation is measuring the assembly rate of a line the deck's own verified artifact says does not loop.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Until a source component is declared, the engine block cannot see the class that binds this deck, and the 9.5% figure it does report describes a kill that is not there.

open_questions.question: The corpus has no section on auditing a combo list — how to price a graph-listed two-card infinite against a verified line — and none on the aristocrats outlet/fodder/converter taxonomy or on -1/-1 counters as removal that pays you.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every card-level judgment in this diagnosis about free versus costed outlets, and about counter annihilation as an anti-synergy, had to be derived from oracle text and one stack artifact rather than cited.

gaps: No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness reports recon absent), so there is no inclusion-rate evidence for what strong Hapatra lists actually run. Every add above is argued from this deck's own artifacts; a recon pass would tell us whether the source class is thin by choice or by oversight.

The in-colour pool contains no second free, repeatable, non-combat -1/-1 source at a fair rate. The only mechanical mirror of Devoted Druid's self-counter untap in B/G is Cinderhaze Wretch at five mana (EDHREC rank 15,571). This is why the prescription is tutor priority and protection rather than an add: the class cannot be deepened by buying a card.

deck-audit emits no axis for the counter-source class, so the constraint this diagnosis names as binding is invisible to all sixteen numbers. It is derived from the goldfish any_of groups plus oracle text plus stack 001, not measured.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256 (freshness reports it as unstamped), so its 19-infinite figure and its Game Changer list are not pinned to the current list the way goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json are.
The audit's engine schema cannot express the UNION of independent kills, so there is no single assembled_rate for 'this deck wins'. The 16.3% and 9.5% figures are per-line and must not be added.
